pages.text: Golden grass sways in the breeze. Leo the lion blinks slowly, watching the savanna wake up around his pride.
Under a shady tree, the pride lounges together. Lions rest many hours to save energy during hot days.
Leo’s ears twitch at distant sounds. He listens for footsteps, birds, and the soft calls of his family.
When the air cools, the pride stands and stretches. Evening is a common time for lions to move and hunt.
Leo lifts his head and roars. The roar tells other lions, “This is our home area—hello, stay away!”
Other lions answer far away. Roars can travel a long distance across open grasslands.
Leo’s pride works as a team. Lions can cooperate, using quiet steps and careful watching.
Lions are carnivores, so they eat meat. After eating, Leo drinks water and returns to shade.
Back at the tree, cubs play and practice pouncing. Play helps young animals learn important skills.
Night arrives softly. Leo lies close to his pride, calm and sleepy, while stars sparkle above the grass.
